limitations: The before and after workloads differ because pre-change failures prevented some CRUD updates; these are controlled observations, not a matched production error-rate experiment.

Cloudflare GraphQL CPU distributions are attributed by time window, not Ray ID. Adaptive sampling, self invocations and background traffic can affect attribution even if counts match. Treat all per-operation CPU windows as estimates.
The isolated health and login windows overlap the browser check and are excluded from comparisons; isolated-health is the replacement health measurement.

Local kernel benchmarks use synthetic 5000-candidate and 3000-point datasets and compare identical outputs. They do not represent full HTTP or production CPU reductions. Zero cold-import CPU readings are below Windows timer resolution.
Detailed Workers Logs API remains 403. Cold starts, real password hashing, SSR and live HTML parsing can still exceed the Workers Free 10ms budget; short successful probes do not guarantee stability.

Successful external geocoding was not exercised without a configured staging key; its success/failure behavior is covered by mocked unit tests. Live candidate HTTP 200 can include upstream warnings or fallback results.
Only staging was deployed and migrated. Production deployment and account billing were not changed. Runtime session/rate-limit/search-cache tables intentionally change during tests.

rollback.database: 0010 only adds indexes; a Worker rollback can retain them. Do not restore a full backup over later edits.
